judged_text: sendAddGuestsEmails sends the full AttendeeScheduledEmail to brand-new guests whose name is the empty string (handler creates attendees with name: ""), while existing attendees get the shorter AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. New guests receive a scheduling confirmation email addressed to a blank name and carrying a duplicate calendar invite (method REQUEST, status CONFIRMED) for an event they never booked; if their mail client already has the event, the blank-name invite confuses the roster, and the new guests get no indication they were added by someone else rather than having booked themselves.

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), the attendee email selection is inverted: for `calendarEvent.attendees`, if `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the normal “you booked”/scheduled confirmation), and otherwise it sends `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (the new “guests added” variant). In the handler, newly created guests are persisted with `name: ""` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts `guestsFullDetails`), so those brand-new guests will receive the scheduled confirmation email addressed with an empty name (and likely a full REQUEST/CONFIRMED invite), rather than the “you were added” messaging (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`). This behavior is directly implied by the diff and is user-visible and incorrect semantics for added guests.
